entry.confirm_signal: 20 repeated interval tones, then 2 tones; the 2 tones say the mode menu is entered
steps: Remove rotor blades or propeller; the motor must stay connected because it makes the tones
Throttle signal at maximum (100 %) before power is applied
Apply supply power; wait for 20 interval tones, then 2 confirmation tones
Throttle to minimum; the ESC sounds mode 1, mode 2, ... in turn

announce.description: The mode number is sounded as that many equal tones (1 to 6). The sequence runs through the modes in order and starts again at mode 1 when no mode is selected. Number of cycles before a restart, tone length and gaps are not stated.

select.description: Throttle to maximum while the wanted mode is being sounded (or just after its tones; the manual does not say which); the ESC answers with 2 tones.

skip.description: No skip. Leaving the throttle at minimum lets the sequence pass every mode; it then restarts at mode 1.

listen.description: After the entry tones the stick goes to minimum, and the ESC sounds the menu while it rests there (entry steps).

store.description: After the selection is answered (2 confirmation tones) the stick goes back to minimum, which stores the mode and arms the ESC (entry steps).

scheme.confirm_signal: 2 tones after selecting at maximum throttle; 2 tones after the return to minimum throttle (armed)
scheme.exit: Throttle to minimum after selection: 2 tones, then the cell-count tones and the arming tones; the ESC is then armed. Power cycle also leaves the menu.
scheme.reset_to_defaults: Selecting a mode sets every parameter of that mode to its default; there is no separate reset.
scheme.description: Power is applied with the throttle at maximum. After 20 interval tones and 2 confirmation tones the throttle goes to minimum and the ESC counts through the modes, one tone count per mode. Throttle to maximum at the wanted count selects it (2 tones). Throttle back to minimum stores it (2 tones) and arms the ESC.

values.name: Governor store (learns the motor parameters at high rpm once)
Motor glider with folding propeller and brake

unknowns: Duration of one tone, gap between tones in a count and pause between two mode counts: not stated
Duration of the 20 interval tones before entry: not stated, so the time from power-on to the 2 confirmation tones is unmeasured
Whether maximum throttle selects during the count or only after the last tone of a count: not stated
Number of times the mode sequence repeats before it ends or restarts: not stated
Minimum supply voltage at which the menu is entered: not stated; ESC cell detection needs a voltage matching the cell count and a 1-20 V bench supply covers at most 4 cells at 4.2 V
Behaviour on a current-limited 3 A bench supply: not stated; the manuals say the ESC is to be powered from batteries only, power supplies are not allowed
Idle current of the ESC with the motor connected: not stated, needed to separate tones from the idle level when counting beeps from supply current
As-delivered mode: not stated for the LVT and Opto models (only the 5-mode family says mode 2 is preprogrammed)

Minimum voltage for Opto 135 (4-12 cells) and Opto 255 (6-16 cells) to start: Opto 255 starts at 6 cells nominal = 25.2 V by cell count, which is above the 20 V bench supply; whether the menu is reachable below that voltage is not stated
Current rating of 135 Slim and Opto 135: not stated as a number
notes: The motor must be connected: the motor windings produce all tones. Without a motor no tones are heard.
Manuals state that the ESC may only be powered from batteries; power supplies are not allowed. The bench supply is outside the manual's intended use.
Power applied with the throttle at maximum enters programming; the manuals tell the user to unplug the battery, set the throttle to minimum and reconnect to leave without changes.
Start-up sequence: 3 descending tones, then cell tones (a long tone counts 5 cells, a short tone 1 cell, e.g. long-long-short-short = 12 cells), then 4 ascending tones at stop throttle.
Mode 1 needs the rpm output wired to a flight controller; mode 3 (Governor store) learns the motor at over 70 % throttle after the first start-up; mode 2 governor works from 50 % throttle.

YGE_35-65LVT_2017_de.pdf covers 35LVT and 65LVT only; YGE_35-95LVT.pdf and YGE_35-95LVT_en.pdf cover 35/65/95LVT; the 135 and Slim appear in YGE_35-135LVT_en.pdf and YGE_35-135LVT_Slim.pdf. All show the same 6-mode menu.
The German LVT editions say the mode setup also learns the throttle range automatically; the English editions do not say so.
YGE_35-95LVT_en.pdf states that with Vbar Control and NEO the mode setup is not needed (auto-detect).
Mode 5 in YGE_Opto255_Navy_en.pdf is labelled Navy; the Navy edition is in yge-mode-setup-navy.
No ProgCard: fine adjustment is by PC setup with a USB adapter (outside stick programming).
